verses.text: When Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her son was dead, she set out to kill the whole royal family.

But Jehosheba, the daughter of King Jehoram and sister of Ahaziah, took Ahaziah's son Joash and secretly took him away from the other princes who were about to be killed. She hid him and his nurse in a bedroom, so Athaliah could not find him, and he was not killed.
Joash stayed hidden with his nurse in the LORD's temple for six years, while Athaliah ruled the land.

In the seventh year, Jehoiada the priest sent for the commanders of units of a hundred, the Carites, and the guards. He brought them to the LORD's temple, made an agreement with them there, and made them swear an oath in the LORD's temple. Then he showed them the king's son.
He gave them these orders: "This is what you must do. One third of you who come on duty on the Sabbath will guard the king's palace.
Another third will be at the Sur Gate, and the last third at the gate behind the guards. You will take turns guarding the temple.
The two groups of you who go off duty on the Sabbath will guard the LORD's temple for the king.
Stand all around the king, each of you with your weapons in your hand. Anyone who comes near your lines must be killed. Stay close to the king wherever he goes."
The commanders of hundreds did everything Jehoiada the priest ordered. Each one took his men, both those coming on duty on the Sabbath and those going off duty, and came to Jehoiada the priest.
The priest gave the commanders the spears and shields that had belonged to King David, which were kept in the LORD's temple.
The guards stood all around the king, each with his weapons in his hand. They stood from the south side of the temple to the north side, near the altar and the temple.

Then Jehoiada brought out the king's son. He put the crown on him and gave him a copy of the covenant. They made him king and anointed him. The people clapped their hands and shouted, "Long live the king!"
When Athaliah heard the noise of the guards and the people, she went to the crowd at the LORD's temple.

She looked and saw the king standing by the pillar, as was the custom. The commanders and trumpeters were beside the king, and all the people of the land were celebrating and blowing trumpets. Then Athaliah tore her clothes and screamed, "Treason! Treason!"

Jehoiada the priest ordered the commanders of hundreds who were in charge of the army, "Bring her out between the lines of soldiers. Kill anyone who follows her." The priest had said, "She must not be killed in the LORD's temple."
So they grabbed her as she went through the horse entrance into the palace grounds, and she was killed there.
Then Jehoiada made a covenant between the LORD and the king and the people, that they would be the LORD's people. He also made an agreement between the king and the people.

All the people of the land went to the temple of Baal and tore it down. They smashed the altars and idols to pieces, and they killed Mattan, the priest of Baal, in front of the altars. Then Jehoiada the priest posted guards at the LORD's temple.

He took the commanders of hundreds, the Carites, the guards, and all the people of the land, and together they led the king down from the LORD's temple. They went through the Gate of the Guards into the palace, and the king took his seat on the royal throne.
All the people of the land celebrated, and the city was calm, because Athaliah had been killed with the sword at the palace.
Joash was seven years old when he became king.
